title: Triage Label Mapping
eyebrow: Proposal · which labels the triage skill uses in this repo

short.lead: The triage skill sorts issues with two kinds of label: a category (bug or enhancement) and a state (needs triage, needs info, ready for agent, ready for human, won't fix). This repo already has 35 labels, but two of the ones you suggested, "in progress" and "needs review", already drive the house-rules design loop: "in progress" means I am building an issue, and "needs review" means it is waiting for your testing. Reusing them for triage would make the hooks read an untriaged issue as one in QA. So this mapping uses labels that nothing else depends on, and adds one new label only where none fits.
short.hint: Tap a row to see which label it uses and why.
items: No existing label means "not looked at yet". Three open issues carry no labels at all today; they would get this one.
"question" is GitHub's default label for an issue waiting on more information. No open issue uses it today.
"up next" reads as "pick this up next" and is used by one open issue. The house rules give it no meaning, so the hooks ignore it.
GitHub's default label for work a person has to take on. No open issue uses it today.
Same name, same meaning. No change.
"bug" is on 49 open issues. For enhancement, "Feature" is on 72 open issues and "enhancement" on 20, so the choice below decides which one triage reads.

changes: Records which repo label stands for each triage role, so every future triage reads it instead of asking.
No mapping exists. Triage stops and asks you to run the setup skill.
A short table maps each of the seven triage roles to one repo label, and names "in progress" and "needs review" as off-limits to triage.

Four new labels are created on GitHub: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent and ready-for-human. wontfix already existed. No existing label is renamed or removed, and no issue is relabelled until you ask for a triage pass.
